outcome: mode of delivery (C/S rate, instrumental vaginal birth, episiotomy)
cohort: The study included 188 pregnant women who regularly attended antenatal classes and subsequently gave birth at an academic tertiary hospital.
finding: Maternal health literacy levels did not significantly impact peripartum and postpartum delivery outcomes, including labor duration and newborn Apgar scores, in pregnant women who attended antenatal classes.
mod_finding: Health literacy levels did not impact mode of delivery; however, the primary cesarean section rate was similar between nulliparous and multiparous groups, potentially indicating that antenatal education services can mitigate the negative impact of low health literacy on cesarean section rates.
